cases.what_created: Temples and palaces in Mesopotamia stored grain and silver for others and lent against it.
cases.source: Homer, S. & Sylla, R., A History of Interest Rates, 4th ed. (Wiley, 2005), early chapters on Mesopotamia; dating is approximate.

cases.what_created: Written laws on loans, interest limits and debt records (Code of Hammurabi).
cases.source: Code of Hammurabi, transl. L. W. King (1910), Yale Avalon Project; date of reign is approximate.

cases.what_created: Medici Bank: branch network across Europe using bills of exchange and double-entry bookkeeping.
cases.source: de Roover, R., The Rise and Decline of the Medici Bank, 1397-1494 (Harvard University Press, 1963).

cases.what_created: Bank of England: a chartered bank created to lend money to the state and issue notes.
cases.source: Bank of England, 'Our history' (the Bank was founded by Royal Charter in 1694); Clapham, J., The Bank of England: A History (1944).

cases.what_created: Panic of 1907: runs on New York trust companies and a near-collapse of the banking system.
A private rescue led by J. P. Morgan and the New York clearing house lent emergency funds to stop the panic.
Federal Reserve Act: created the US central bank as lender of last resort.
1920s credit boom: the number of US banks peaked at roughly 30,000 and lending to stock buyers grew quickly.
cases.source: Friedman, M. & Schwartz, A., A Monetary History of the United States, 1867-1960 (Princeton, 1963); exact peak year is approximate.

cases.what_created: Stock market crash and a wave of bank failures through 1933.
cases.source: Friedman, M. & Schwartz, A., A Monetary History of the United States, 1867-1960 (Princeton, 1963).

cases.what_created: National bank holiday and Emergency Banking Act: banks closed, inspected, then reopened.
Banking Act of 1933 (Glass-Steagall): deposit insurance (FDIC) and separation of commercial and investment banking.
cases.source: Federal Reserve History, 'Banking Act of 1933, Glass-Steagall'.

cases.what_created: Global financial crisis: Lehman Brothers failed and credit markets froze.
cases.source: Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission, Final Report (2011).

cases.what_created: Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP): government capital injections into banks.
cases.source: Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-343), US Treasury.

cases.what_created: Bitcoin network launched: a way to move value without a bank in the middle.
cases.source: Nakamoto, S., 'Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System' (2008); first block mined January 2009.

cases.what_created: Dodd-Frank Act: new bank capital rules, a consumer protection bureau and resolution powers.
cases.source: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, Public Law 111-203 (2010).
